title: Add deterministic replay + canary guardrail for autoscaler rollout regressions causing queue starvation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer escalations from three tenants (two hosted, one private) surfaced intermittent high p99 for short requests during multi-hour bursts of long-context generation. Investigations found a correlation between a new autoscaler rollout (burst-policy changes) and the scheduler's batch formation heuristics: large, long-context requests were pinned to GPUs for extended KV-cache lifetimes and caused small, latency-sensitive requests to queue up (observed as queue starvation and tail-latency spikes). This ticket scopes a patch and operational guardrails: (1) build a deterministic replay harness that can reproduce production traffic mixes including KV-cache checkpoint states, (2) add a canary-level check in autoscaler/rollout pipelines that runs the harness and validates latency fairness and no regression in short-request p50/p95/p99, and (3) ship a short-term scheduler mitigation (bounded preemption + per-tenant short-request fastlane) to unblock customers while long-term fixes are validated.
root_cause_summary: The autoscaler rollout introduced a burst policy that increased packing of long-context requests onto fewer GPUs without adjusting scheduler preemption and continuous-batching fairness knobs. Long requests held KV state and GPU occupancy longer than expected; continuous batching merged heterogeneous-length requests leading to head-of-line effects for short requests. Under certain mixes, backlog amplification and delayed preemption resulted in sustained queue starvation for short flows.
proposed_solution: 1) Deterministic replay harness: record representative production request signatures (length distribution, model variant, tenant priority) and a synthetic KV state snapshot to replay scheduling decisions locally and in CI. 2) Canary guardrail: integrate harness into rollout pipeline — fail rollouts that increase short-request p99 by >15% or introduce >10% new queue-stall events in a 30-minute synthetic run. 3) Short-term mitigation: implement timeboxed preemption token and a "fastlane" queue for requests <128 tokens that bypasses large-request batching when saturation detected. 4) Observability: add per-tenant queue starvation counters and a synthetic-run dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic replay harness can reproduce the customer-observed latency spike in our staging cluster within 1.5x of prod p99 for short requests
CI guardrail runs as part of autoscaler rollouts and fails candidate canaries that worsen short-request p99 by >15%
Short-term mitigation (preemption token + fastlane) is deployed behind a feature flag and reduces short-request p99 by at least 40% in affected mixes
Dashboard shows synthetic-run results and per-tenant starvation metrics; on-call runbook updated with rollback and mitigation steps
Customer follow-ups: affected tenants confirm improved tail latency in a staged canary and are notified of the rollback-free resolution
updates: 2025-02-10 - Triage: Escalation call with SRE, runtime, and support. Collected stack traces, sample requests, and affected tenant IDs. Created minimal reproducer from one hosted tenant.

2025-02-12 - Investigation: Found autoscaler change (burst_policy_v2) deployed two days before first report. Observed GPU packing metric increase and longer KV cache lifetimes. Reproduced queue-stall locally with synthetic long-context stream and mixed short requests.

2025-02-14 - Decision: Prioritize deterministic replay harness + CI guardrail. Short-term mitigation accepted: preemption token + fastlane behind feature flag. Owner: Ethan Morales. Dependencies: infra permission to snapshot synthetic KV state in staging.

2025-02-16 - Patch: Prototype preemption token implemented (runtime-level hook) and fastlane scheduler path added. Unit tests and basic e2e harness pass locally. Filed PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4678

2025-02-18 - Canary: Deployed feature-flagged mitigation to 10% of Dedicated capacity and 5% of Hosted canaries. Early signals: short-request p99 down ~35% in canary; no impact on throughput for long-context flows observed so far. Added extra tracing for KV checkpoint handoff.

2025-02-20 - Ongoing: Building deterministic replay harness and integrating into CI. Draft runbook and rollback instructions posted. Customer comms prepared; support triage remains open until full canary pass. Next: finish harness, add automated failure criterion, widen canary.
Reviewer feedback: PM requested clear metric thresholds and customer-facing timeline. Security asked whether synthetic KV snapshots include any PII (they do not; all payloads are signature-only).
resolution_notes: (work in progress) Short-term mitigation deployed to canary; observed ~35% p99 improvement for short requests. Deterministic harness in alpha and will gate broader rollout. Final resolution will include permanent fairness knobs in scheduler and CI guardrail for autoscaler rollouts to prevent regression recurrence.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add autoscaler rollout gate for scheduling fairness tests. 2) Harden continuous-batching heuristics to avoid merging sub-128 token requests with >2048 token requests when system saturation detected. 3) Create synthetic workload library representing top 10 tenant mixes. 4) Customer outreach and SLA credit review if needed.
notes: Avoided immediate global rollback because mitigation reduces short-request tail without hurting throughput. Trade-off: small throughput loss for long-context flows in extreme synthetic tests; acceptable for canary but requires tuning before full rollout.
